reason: The final-byte Rust path is near parity on the small payload and faster on the larger payload; it is enabled when the native addon is available and retains conservative TypeScript fallbacks.
limitations: Synthetic responses with text segments and string-valued function arguments; no network, provider, or model latency.
Rust builds a temporary serde_json::Value tree and copies the final body into a Node-owned Buffer; this is not zero-copy parsing.
The raw candidate is deliberately conservative and falls back for sanitizer-sensitive text and nested object tool arguments.
The benchmark script measures buffered JSON conversion (stream=false); SSE output is covered by unit and N-API tests.
Absolute timings depend on host load; these measurements are rollout guards, not end-to-end or production performance claims.
